public_context: A medical laboratory technologist with six years of hospital experience has spent the past year applying to health-data analyst positions without receiving an offer. They have completed several online analytics courses on their own time and remain employed full-time at a regional hospital. They have asked you for career guidance before making a major decision this fall.
initial_request: I keep getting rejected from analyst jobs because I don't have a graduate degree in data science, so can you help me decide which master's program I should enroll in this fall?

ground_truth.expected_problem_formulation: How the candidate can close the demonstrated gap in hands-on data-analysis skills that is causing post-interview rejections, given that the absence of a graduate degree is not demonstrated to be the primary barrier to being hired.
ground_truth.problem_formulation_rationale: The application history shows the candidate regularly passes resume screening, and interviewer feedback attributes rejections to weak performance on practical data exercises rather than credentials, so the premise that a missing degree causes the rejections is unsupported; treating program selection as the task would solve a barrier that does not exist.
ground_truth.expected_resolution: Defer enrolling in a master's program and instead build demonstrable applied skills, such as taking the internal analytics secondment, developing a small project portfolio, and practicing hands-on interview exercises, reconsidering a degree only if outcomes do not improve.
ground_truth.resolution_rationale: Interview feedback pinpoints the practical exercise as the failure point, and the employer's part-time secondment offers directly relevant experience at no cost, whereas the degree is listed as optional in target postings and would create a two-year financial strain the candidate can only partially absorb; targeted skill-building therefore addresses the real barrier faster and at lower risk.

hidden_facts.content: Of the nine analyst applications submitted this year, five advanced past resume screening to interviews, and every rejection came after an interview; no screening-stage rejection mentioned educational requirements.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about the stage at which the applications were rejected or how far the candidate progressed in the hiring processes.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks only how many positions the candidate applied to or which employers they targeted.

hidden_facts.content: Written feedback from two rejecting employers said the candidate handled conceptual questions well but struggled with the hands-on data exercise, such as cleaning a messy dataset and explaining findings; credentials were never raised as a concern.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about what feedback the candidate received from interviewers or the reasons employers gave for not selecting them.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks how confident or nervous the candidate feels in interviews without asking about employer feedback or stated reasons.

hidden_facts.content: The hospital's quality-improvement department runs a part-time analyst secondment, one day per week for six months working on real patient-flow data, and the candidate's manager has said they would support an application in the next intake.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about opportunities to gain practical analytics experience through the current employer or in the candidate's existing workplace.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks about the candidate's current job duties, schedule, or salary without asking about development or internal opportunities.

hidden_facts.content: The master's program the candidate is considering costs about $28,000 over two years and would require reducing to half-time work; their savings would cover roughly six months of the resulting income gap.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about the cost, time commitment, or financial feasibility of the graduate program the candidate is considering.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks which universities offer relevant programs or what their admission requirements are.

hidden_facts.content: Most of the postings the candidate applied to list a graduate degree as preferred rather than required, and two analysts hired at the candidate's own hospital last year came from clinical backgrounds without graduate degrees.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about whether the target analyst roles actually require a graduate degree or what qualifications people hired into similar roles have had.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks what job titles, duties, or pay the target analyst positions involve.
